newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-REAL FACE MAKE-OR-BREAK WEEK OF CUP AND LEAGUE ACTION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-REAL FACE MAKE-OR-BREAK WEEK OF CUP AND LEAGUE ACTION.

text.p: After failing to get more than a point at bottom-placed Extremadura, Fabio Capello's Real Madrid face what could prove to be a make-or-break week of league and Cup action.

Real will defend a slender 2-1 advantage at surprise outfit Valladolid in the second round of their Spanish Cup tie on Wednesday, before travelling to neighbours Atletico for Saturday's vital championship clash.
Real's goalless draw at Extremadura contrasted with the 4-2 victory chalked up by Atletico at the same ground the previous week.
The Barcelona-based daily 'Sport' gloatingly called the result 'ridiculous', and reminded its readers that Barca stood to knock Real off the top spot by winning Monday night's game with Hercules.
Once again Capello came in for criticism, this time for substituting Croatian striker Davor Suker.
But after a week in which Real had been dubbed 'lucky' by Barcelona players, the former AC Milan coach was quick to go on the offensive.
"And they say we're lucky. If that's luck .." demanded Capello, listing the chances his players had squandered.
But Extremadura had also wasted a series of last-gasp pporutunities to take what would have been an historic win.
Even so fans treated the draw as a famous victory after being slighted by press coverage which seemed to belittle not only their team, but also their town.

An article in the Madrid-based sports daily 'Marca' contrasting the wealth of the mighty six-times European champions with the more modest resources of the first division newboys particularly excited the wrath of supporters.
On Sunday 'Marca' published an apology and a piece headed 'Almendralejo, capital of Spain', but the only copies of the newspaper that sold in the town that day were used for a bonfire lit in protest.
During the game fans waved banners which listed the virtues of Almendralejo and described the remote, 25,000-population rural town as an 'international city'.
Real's next destination, Valladolid, was indeed once the capital of Spain, but has never found much of a place on the country's footballing maps.
The team seemed doomed to relegation just a year ago. But the return of coach Vicente Cantatore lifted the side off the bottom, and this season Valladolid are riding high in seventh.
With sharpshooting Croatian striker Alen Peternac back from suspension, Valladolid need just a 1-0 victory to knock Real out of the Cup before the semi-finals for the second year in succession.
Cup holders Atletico -- who are still involved in Europe and have a bye in this round -- are very much the team in form after clocking up their tenth game without defeat by demolishing Zaragoza 5-1.

The champions' return to form after a rocky start has coincided with the reappearance of playmaker Jose Luis Caminero. Caminero opened the scoring on Sunday after just 30 seconds, but was injured in the process and is once again doubtful for the game against his old club.
Caminero was sent off in last year's game at Real, and missed the return match at the Vicente Calderon stadium because of suspension.
